instantiated_cells.justification: Section 13.66 bars anyone from lobbying as a lobbyist unless licensed under §13.63 and authorized under §13.65, making lobbyist licensing/registration a legal prerequisite to lobbying.
A lobbyist license expires on December 31 of each even-numbered year, which corresponds to a biennial (24-month) renewal cadence.
The statute separately requires lobbyists to obtain a license (§13.63) and principals/clients to register (§13.64), with a separate written authorization filed for each principal (§13.65).
Section 13.63 specifies required items for a lobbyist license application (including SSN/oath statement and signature) but does not require submission of a photograph.
Elective state officials, local/tribal officials, and legislative employees are not subject to specified lobbying provisions when acting in an official capacity.

An agency filing a statement under §13.695 and named officials are exempt from several lobbying provisions (e.g., licensing/registration/reporting) except as provided in §13.695, creating a partial exemption for government agencies.

unscoreable_emissions.reason: The bundled provisions describe license application contents and expirations but do not state any general deadline for lobbyists to amend/update their own license application information.

The statute requires a lobbyist to be licensed before lobbying (§13.66) but does not provide a 'days after first lobbying' registration window; the CPI question’s numeric deadline is therefore not stated as such in the text.
